messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 09 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Market flags & proposed action list for Jan QBR

Team —

Quick, high-level flags we need on the QBR slide deck and the leadership one-pager. I captured the items below and attached a short 1-pager (market-flags-summary.pdf). Please do two things: (1) add any missing competitor facts to the shared Drive doc linked below, and (2) claim an owner for each ask via reply-all.

Top-line flags (urgent):
- HelixAI: launched "Helix-XL" last week with public pricing tiers and aggressive entry discounts (see attached). Early field notes indicate Helix is marketing 30–40% cost advantage for multi-instance inference.
- CloudSphere: beta for "spot-inference" — claims up to 50% savings for bursty workloads but with higher cold-start variability.
- Open-model releases: two mid-sized models (Mistral-Delta and Northwind-13B) surfaced in community channels; both are being bundled by some vendors as lower-cost, near-production alternatives.
- Positioning shifts: a growing trend to sell "throughput economics" instead of raw per-token pricing (bundled inference units, committed bursts).

Proposed actionables for QBR and OKR implications:
1) Pricing competitive slide: Laura to own a one-slide comparison of list vs. effective price (include batch/caching assumptions).
2) Field memo + messaging: Markus to propose concise rebuttal messaging for customers (quick FAQ + 2x talking points).
3) Model onboarding watchlist: Karthik to propose which model variants we should certify for Dedicated in next 60 days.
4) Rapid win: identify 3 at-risk deals where a short-term discount/commitment structure prevents churn (list in HS).

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2bMarketFlags_QBR
Attachment: market-flags-summary.pdf (2 pages)

Thanks — please reply with owners and any additional flags by EOD today.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP Product & Strategy | Redwood Inference
